In the 80s, I had the chance to play an Irish wake in Dorchester, MA. It was in a hall, not far from Duddly Street.

I don't think I've ever played more drunkenly than I played that night. It was oh so stereotypical - but it gets even better. Before too long (time flies when you're drunk) we were no longer on the stage. The "mourners" had pretty much commandeered our instruments, someone had dug out a pipe from somewhere, and we had all these old people playing traditional Irish folk on our little stage - all while we were getting paid to get drunk and not play! Someone even dug an accordion out of their car. Who carries one of those in their car? The Irish mob, that's who.

We'd sometimes swap back in with them and a few people would meander on and off the stage in some sort of non-organized rotation. It was kind of like just come play a song and we'll all try to keep up. Even the younger crowd got in on it. Of the couple hundred people at the wake, I'd say probably 50 of them made it on the stage at one point or another. We started at about 15:00 and we kept going until the following morning at about 05:00.

When I say I'd rather play a wake than play a wedding, that's exactly what I am referring to.
